neighbours.label: The slot where a survey response category begins in a poll statistic ('X% rated it as', 'say they are very', 'called it "very ..."'), vs the same judgment words from one person outside a poll
fire: In the survey, 52% of nurses rated their workload as heavy or very heavy.
Just 12 percent of young voters say they are very satisfied with Congress.
Two in five farmers polled described the harvest as below average.
A third of employees called their manager "very supportive" in the poll.
Among those polled, 64% said the plan was somewhat or very likely to fail.
Only 9% of residents consider crime "not a problem" in their area.
The state's corn crop was rated 48 percent good to excellent this week.
Of the teachers surveyed, 30% felt extremely stressed during the year.
quiet: The doctor described her injury as minor and sent her home.
The critic called the new restaurant "very expensive" in his review.
My grandmother says she is very happy in her new flat.
The inspector rated the old boiler as unsafe and shut it down.
He felt extremely tired after the long night shift.
The coach said the team was very likely to win on Sunday.
Our neighbor considers the noise a big problem at night.
The farmer described the harvest as poor after the drought.

predictions: Poll-statistic sentences reach 0.5-0.8 at as/very/extremely/quote; one person's judgment with the same words stays under 0.2.
notes: Probe: 'program was "very helpful"' (surveyed parents) 0.785, '41% ... economy as poor' 0.761, '30% rated the service as' 0.690, '18 percent ... extremely confident' 0.498; 'engineers described as unsafe' 0.137, 'weather was extremely cold' 0.010. Near misses keep the rating words and drop the poll.
